cards.text: Welcome in, friend. This passage opens with a word I wish it didn't: Again. Again the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD, so He delivered them into the hand of Midian.

cards.question: Israel stays in the hand of Midian for ___ years.

cards.text: The hand of Midian prevails against Israel. It gets so bad that the Israelites start preparing shelters for themselves.

cards.question: Because of the Midianites, where do the Israelites prepare their shelters?

answers.text: Up in the mountains and caves

cards.text: Here's the pattern. Whenever Israel plants crops, the Midianites, Amalekites and other people of the east come up and invade.

cards.question: The invaders camp against Israel as far as Gaza and ___ the produce of the land.

cards.text: They leave Israel nothing to live on, not even sheep, oxen or donkeys. That's like pulling a fresh batch out of the oven, turning around for ONE second, and finding an empty cooling rack, EVERY single harvest!

cards.question: The Midianites pour in with their livestock and their tents. What does the Bible say they come in like?
True or false: the Midianites and their camels could be counted.

cards.text: Israel is greatly impoverished by Midian. So the Israelites cry out to the LORD.

cards.question: When Israel cries out because of Midian, the LORD sends them a ___ with a message.

cards.text: The message starts with what the LORD has done. He brought them up out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, and He drove out their oppressors and gave them their land.

cards.question: Then the LORD reminds Israel of something He told them. What was it?

answers.text: Not to fear the gods of the Amorites
Not to make peace with the Midianites
Not to plant their crops near Gaza

cards.question: True or false: in the prophet's message, the LORD says Israel obeyed Him.

cards.text: Then the angel of the LORD comes and sits under the oak in Ophrah that belongs to Joash the Abiezrite. And right there, Joash's son Gideon is threshing wheat, hiding it from the Midianites.

cards.question: Where is Gideon threshing his wheat to hide it from the Midianites?
The angel of the LORD appears to Gideon and tells him the LORD is with him. What does the angel call Gideon?

cards.text: If an angel called ME a mighty man of valor while I was lying in that junk drawer, I'd have turned around to see who he was talking to! Gideon answers, “Please, my Lord, if the LORD is with us, why has all this happened to us?”

cards.question: Gideon asks where all the LORD's wonders went. Which wonder does he say his fathers told him about?

answers.text: Bringing them up out of Egypt

cards.question: True or false: Gideon tells the angel that the LORD has forsaken Israel and handed them over to Midian.

cards.text: Gideon has just asked where the LORD's wonders went. Then the LORD turns to him.

cards.question: The LORD turns to Gideon and gives him a job. What is it?

cards.text: The LORD tells him to go in the strength he has, and asks, “Am I not sending you?” I bet Gideon checks that strength like a bank account the day before payday.

cards.question: Gideon asks how he can save Israel. He says his clan is the ___ in Manasseh.
True or false: Gideon says he is the oldest in his father's house.

cards.text: The LORD replies, “Surely I will be with you, and you will strike down all the Midianites as one man.”
But Gideon wants to be sure who he's talking to.

cards.question: Gideon asks for a ___ that it's really the LORD speaking with him.

cards.text: He asks Him not to leave until he comes back with an offering. And the LORD says, “I will stay until you return.”

cards.question: Gideon goes in and gets his offering ready. What does he bring out under the oak?

answers.text: A young goat and unleavened bread
A lamb and a jar of honey
A dove and a jar of oil

cards.text: The angel of God tells him to lay the meat and the unleavened bread on this rock and pour out the broth. And Gideon does it.

cards.question: The angel of the LORD touches the meat and the bread with the tip of his staff. What happens?

answers.text: Fire flares up from the rock
Water pours out of the rock
The rock splits right in two

cards.question: True or false: after the fire, the angel of the LORD stays right there in Gideon's sight.

cards.text: That's when Gideon realizes it was the angel of the LORD. It's like griping to a nice stranger in the elevator about how the company's run, and then he walks into your meeting and sits at the head of the table.

cards.question: Gideon cries out, “Oh no, Lord GOD!” What does he say happened?

answers.text: He saw the angel face to face
He has no sword to fight with
He has no army to lead

cards.question: The LORD says to him, “Peace be with you. Do not be afraid,” True or false: the LORD tells Gideon he will not die.

cards.text: So Gideon builds an altar to the LORD right there. The text says it still stands in Ophrah of the Abiezrites to this day.

cards.question: What does Gideon call the altar he builds in Ophrah?

cards.text: On that very night, the LORD speaks to Gideon again. And this job is a whole lot closer to home.

cards.question: What does the LORD tell Gideon to tear down?

cards.text: He's to take two of his father's bulls, the second one seven years old, and cut down the Asherah pole beside Baal's altar. Then he builds a proper altar to the LORD on top of this stronghold.

cards.question: Gideon is to offer the second bull as a burnt offering, using the wood of the ___ he cut down.

cards.text: So Gideon takes ten of his servants and does what the LORD told him.

cards.question: True or false: Gideon and his servants do the job in broad daylight.
Why does Gideon tear down Baal's altar at night?

answers.text: He fears his father's household and the city
The LORD told him to keep it all a secret
His servants could only work after dark

cards.text: Morning comes, and the men of the city get up. One night and ten servants, friend, and it took ME years and an angel to get out of one drawer!

cards.question: True or false: when the men of the city get up in the morning, Baal's altar is still standing.

cards.text: “Who did this?” they say to one another. They investigate thoroughly, and they're told, “Gideon son of Joash did it.”

cards.question: The men of the city tell Joash to bring out his son. They say Gideon must ___.

cards.text: Now Joash has a whole crowd standing against him. It's like waking up to fifty notifications from the neighborhood group chat, and EVERY one of them is about your kid.

cards.question: True or false: Joash hands Gideon over to the men of the city.

cards.text: Joash asks them, “Are you contending for Baal? Are you trying to save him?” Then he warns that whoever pleads Baal's case will be put to death by morning.

cards.question: Joash tells the crowd what Baal should do if Baal is a god. What is it?

cards.text: So on that day, Gideon gets a new name: Jerubbaal.

cards.question: Gideon is called Jerubbaal because he tore down Baal's altar. What does Jerubbaal mean?

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend. The guy from the winepress has a brand new name, and trust me, his story is just getting warmed up.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 18 quotes "Please, my Lord, if the LORD is with us, why has all this happened to us?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 6 quotes "Surely I will be with you, and you will strike down all the Midianites as one man.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Midian is the first new people group in the passage, and they appear here without saying who they are. Card 5 later adds the Amalekites without introducing them either.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The joke compares Israel's loss to a batch vanishing from the cooling rack, then ends with "EVERY single harvest!" That pulls the Bible setting (harvest) into the cookie image and blends the two.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The card retells 6:13 ("Gideon has just asked where the LORD's wonders went") but cites only 6:14. That opening line is also a recap of the previous stop.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The first sentence only recaps what the baker already saw in stop 1. It doesn't move the passage forward.
The bank-account-before-payday joke tells the baker that Gideon sees his strength as low. That gives away card 4's answer ("weakest" over "richest" and "largest").

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Card 14 has just told the baker that Gideon realizes it was the angel of the LORD. Both wrong answers (no sword, no army) have nothing to do with that realization, so the setup rules them out and the right answer stands out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: "Two of his father's bulls" settles something the text leaves open. Verse 6:25 says "your father's young bull and a second bull seven years old" and never says whose the second bull is.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card packs in three things: taking the two bulls, cutting down the Asherah pole, and building the altar to the LORD.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: Card 3 just said Gideon is to "cut down the Asherah pole," and this blank asks for "the ___ he cut down." The story card gives the answer away.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: "winepress" doesn't fit "the ___ he cut down," because a winepress isn't something you cut down. It isn't the same kind of thing as the other answers, and it's easy to dismiss.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The joke compares Gideon tearing down and building altars in one night with Papa Dorin escaping the drawer over years. Those aren't the same action, so the comparison doesn't click.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The group-chat joke is a parenting scenario ("EVERY one of them is about your kid").

rule.text: No jokes or scenarios about school, parents or anything aimed at kids. Work, bosses and bills are fine.
